title: Telemetry shape-signalling proxy for polymorphic schema adaptation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight proxy layer in the Console backend ingestion path that performs 'shape-signalling' for telemetry envelopes. Purpose: make telemetry schema evolution tolerant by letting clients (SDK / CLI / internal API callers) signal the observed payload shape while the proxy performs minimal, safe adaptation or routes unfamiliar shapes for safe capture and analysis. This reduces ingestion errors during client rollouts and enables staged schema migrations without broad client churn.
motivation: Recent rollouts have shown brittle failures when clients send new fields or restructure event envelopes. Full schema negotiation across SDK/CLI/API surface is slow and error-prone. A proxy that emits a compact shape token and can adapt or route unknown shapes allows incremental server-side compatibility and faster rollouts for SDK/CLI and internal integrations.
goals: Add a proxy component that computes a deterministic 'shape_token' for each telemetry envelope
Surface 'X-Telemetry-Shape' header to downstream pipelines and storage
Provide runtime adaptors for a set of backwards-compatible transforms (field rename, nested flattening, optional->nullable)
Implement a capture-and-quarantine path for unknown shapes and automatic alerting
Define rollout plan: SDK opt-in header -> server-side canary -> bulk rollout with monitoring
acceptance_criteria: Proxy emits shape_token for 100% of accepted events in canary cluster
When shape matches a known adaptor rule, event is transformed and ingested without schema validation failures
Unknown shapes are written to a quarantine bucket and produce an alert to #telemetry-monitoring with sample payloads
SDK and CLI changes are backwards compatible; clients that do not include shape header still get a derived token from the proxy
End-to-end tests and contract tests added to the telemetry CI suite
design_decisions: Use a compact deterministic hashing approach (ordered key traversal + type markers) to compute shape_token rather than full structural diff to keep tokens stable across benign changes
Keep proxies stateless; adaptation rules live in a versioned ruleset stored in S3 with atomic fetch semantics
Do not attempt to rewrite deeply incompatible events; route them to quarantine to avoid data corruption
Expose shape metadata as an HTTP header (X-Telemetry-Shape) and as top-level envelope metadata for downstream processors
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy proxy to canary ingestion cluster behind feature-flag; proxy computes shape_token but performs no transforms
Phase 1: enable a small set of adaptors (rename email->user_email, flatten session.id) in canary and validate downstream dashboards
Phase 2: SDK and CLI release with optional header to allow client-side signalling; continue server-side derivation for older clients
Phase 3: expand adaptor rules for common migrations and enable on 50% of production traffic
Phase 4: full rollout after 72h stability and metric thresholds met (error rate < baseline + 0.1%)
monitoring_and_metrics: ingest validation error rate by shape_token
latency 95/99 for proxy added path (must be < 5ms p95 additional)
tests: Deterministic shape_token unit tests for a broad set of synthesized envelopes
Adaptor integration tests verifying canonical transforms preserve downstream semantics
Contract tests for SDK/CLI header handshake and header-absent derivation
Chaos test: inject malformed but syntactically valid shapes and validate quarantine behavior
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: token instability on reorderings -> Mitigation: canonical key ordering and type markers
Risk: adaptor rules mismap fields -> Mitigation: staged canary + automated golden comparisons against pre-migration store
Risk: added latency -> Mitigation: highly optimized Go proxy, local signature cache, p95 target 5ms
Risk: spikes of unknown shapes during major SDK rollouts -> Mitigation: auto-throttle client rollouts and revert transforms remotely
implementation_notes: Proxy implemented as a sidecarless Go microservice that accepts same ingress contracts as current gateway
Ruleset published as versioned JSON-LD-like artifacts; proxy fetches new rules atomically and logs rule version in telemetry
Provide a lightweight CLI tooling to compute shape_token locally for SDK maintainers (telemetry-shape tool)
Store quarantined samples in S3 with lifecycle policy and an automatic job that extracts representative samples daily

notes: Keep client-facing schema docs unchanged; this server-side proxy is an implementation detail to reduce breakage during migration windows.
We intentionally avoid deep synthetic rewrites; aim for safe normalizations only (rename/flatten/nullable).
Follow-on work: add a 'shape diff' generator service to produce candidate adaptor rules from quarantined payload clusters (productized later).
